execution_steps: 1. After the Stop hook flagged FF6-EVENT-000275 (oracle machinery fix) as product-work-free, surveyed nrrd (Event 276, space-consistency wiring) then xliff's 21 remaining unresolved obligations directly via the implementation-evidence ledger, applying this session's own established discipline of reading each obligation's own precise wording rather than trusting its missing_behavior summary.

2. Found 10 of 21 xliff obligations sharing near-identical missing_behavior text claiming 'no schema, Schematron, or NVDL files are vendored anywhere in this repository' -- but this session's own Event 270/272 already bundled the module XSDs, directly contradicting that claim for the XSD portion. Suspected the same staleness might apply to the Schematron/NVDL portion too.

3. Checked whether src-xlf-002.bin (the ZIP already mined at Event 272) contains anything beyond the *.xsd entries previously extracted: zipfile.namelist() showed 9 *.sch files and 1 *.nvdl file present in the archive, none previously extracted.

4. Extracted all 10 files into the existing validation/schemas/ directory alongside the module XSDs. Confirmed file counts and names against each of the three distinct obligation rule_text claims before writing any code: 'exactly nine Schematron rule sets' (core xliff_core_2.1.sch + 8 of 9 modules, ITS Mapping has none), 'an NVDL advanced-validation dispatch artifact' (1 file), 'exactly nine first-party module XSDs' (already had these from Event 272).

5. Attempted to determine whether real Schematron rule EXECUTION was newly feasible (lxml.isoschematron.Schematron is available in this environment) before assuming inventory-only was the ceiling. Empirically tested all nine .sch files: every one fails to load with 'This implementation of ISO Schematron does not work with schemas using the xslt2 query language.' Confirmed via direct queryBinding grep that the core file declares xslt2 explicitly; the eight module files inherit or resolve it the same way (empirically confirmed by the identical failure, not merely assumed from the core's own attribute). This is a genuine, confirmed toolchain gap, not an oversight -- running these would need a Java-based or other XSLT-2-capable Schematron processor this environment does not have.

6. Added bundled_schematron_paths() and bundled_nvdl_path() to schema_validator.py, returning real file paths for a caller with a capable external processor to use -- honest about not offering execution itself, consistent with the module's own existing docstring pattern for the schema_validate()/full_schema_validate() split.
7. Updated pyproject.toml package-data to include schemas/*.sch and schemas/*.nvdl.

8. Wrote 7 tests: exact Schematron file count, exact module coverage (core + 8 modules, itsm absent), NVDL presence, exact module XSD count/coverage (locking in what Event 272's own test only proved as a subset check), well-formedness of every bundled .sch/.nvdl file, and a dedicated test asserting lxml.isoschematron's own XSLTApplyError on the core file -- this last test is deliberately a REGRESSION TRIP-WIRE: if a future lxml/libxslt upgrade ever adds XSLT2 support, this test starts failing, which is the correct signal to revisit real Schematron execution.
9. Ran the full xliff suite (530 -> 537 passed), ruff (clean), and mypy --strict (25 source files, clean).
10. Built a real wheel via `pip wheel . --no-deps` and confirmed all 10 new files ship inside it under format_factory/xliff/validation/schemas/, byte-identical to source.

11. Updated the implementation-evidence ledger for all 9 target obligations (status, source_symbols, positive_test_selectors, execution_evidence_ids, implemented_behavior, missing_behavior) plus a new dedicated evidence entry, validating the YAML parses correctly and the obligation/evidence counts match expectations (142 obligations unchanged, evidence 46->47) after every edit.
